messages:
emma: Heads up — BetaCorp POC stuck during tenant setup. SCIM returns 401 unauthenticated and SAML assertions fail upstream with 'Unknown NameID policy'. They're migrating from Hosted -> Dedicated + VPC. Need quick triage and remediation steps.
dan: ok — can you paste the last scim-proxy error and the SAML NameID snippet? Also tell me which API key they entered in the Dedicated console.
priya: quick note: Dedicated tenant keys are issued with a tenant claim baked into the token and must be used against the /dedicated/<tenant> scim path. Hosted keys will 401 if used there.
emma: logs (redacted):
```
scim-proxy: 401 unauthorized - token missing tenant claim
scim-proxy: upstream returned 400 invalid_payload -> okta sent emails[0].type instead of emails[0].value
saml-service: NameIDPolicy refused: "urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:unspecified"
```
dan: sounds like three things: wrong key, attribute shape mismatch, and NameID policy unspecified which some IdPs block by policy. Ask IdP to set NameID format to emailAddress or add an explicit NameID in the app mapping.
priya: check if BetaCorp pasted a hosted key. Also their SCIM connector URL must be exactly `https://scim.redwood.company/dedicated/betacorp/Users`. Any trailing slash or path mismatch will cause token audience check to fail.
emma: they pasted a token that starts with "rudx-" (looks like hosted). They also said their Okta template uses a legacy SCIM mapping and toggles 'Send emails as array' which changed the payload shape.
dan: recommended immediate fixes: 1) issue a short-lived tenant-scoped token and DM it for immediate provisioning; 2) ask IdP to change NameID format to emailAddress (or map email to an attribute); 3) update SCIM mapping to accept emails[0].value or switch Okta to simple email property.
priya: I'll create a temp token: `rudx-tenant-temp-betacorp-4h`. Also adding a short-term proxy rule to accept emails array to prevent provisioning pause. Rolling that in now.
emma: thank you. Also BetaCorp's security team asked about IP allowlisting since they're on a VPC — they want to ensure ACS callback comes from our peering endpoint. Can we confirm ACS origin IP?
dan: we provide metadata with ACS url; the ACS endpoint is behind our LB (lb-redwood-internal) with stable egress IPs for SAML callback. I'll DM the egress CIDR list; for tight security they can allow the CIDR or configure SAML handshake through the peering connection.
provisioning-bot: issued temporary token rudx-tenant-temp-betacorp-4h valid until 2147460900.
priya: rolled proxy patch to accept emails[0].value (hotfix) and restarted deployment: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/scim-proxy -n prod`.
emma: BetaCorp retested — scim 201 Created and users appear. SAML login still failing with NameIDPolicy refused because their Org policy forbids email NameID for some apps.
dan: if their org blocks email NameID, ask them to create a dedicated SAML app for Redwood and set NameID to persistent or provide a stable attribute to map (e.g., employeeId). We'll need an attribute mapping in our SAML handler to use that attribute as the canonical email for SCIM linking.
emms: (typo) emma: typo above — they chose employeeId and mapped it. After mapping employeeId -> our 'external_id' field and switching SCIM mapping to match, provisioning + login succeed.
provisioning-bot: SCIM sync 6621 finished: 42 created, 5 updated, 0 errors.
emma: BetaCorp confirmed POC access, thanks team. Follow-up: docs task to add a short section on 'Hosted vs Dedicated keys and SCIM path mismatches' and a UI validation to detect hosted-key paste into Dedicated console. Closing thread. :rocket:
